decisions.detail: 'Identify the third side, the parallel lines and the similar triangle in a triangle in which the mid-points of two sides are marked.' Only exercise evidence (10 items); one of the two rule failures of this chapter (rule 1).
decisions.basis: ORCHESTRATOR (AI) RULING, not a human stamp and not in the auto-pass rule set: section 7.4 never teaches identifying the third side, the parallel lines or the similar triangle as a skill. Its teaching text is one subject, the mid-point theorem: a heading (EMA66), the paper-cutting activity (b02950), WE8 (the proof), the converse (b02952-b02954) and the chapter summary's statement of the theorem (b03019). There is no worked example, definition or explanation of reading the third side or the parallel pair off a figure, and similar-triangle notation is taught in section 7.2 (b02845-b02848, lesson g10m7s2-1, lo-3), not in this lesson. The run's merged evidence for this objective is three exercises (Ex7-7:1, 3, 5b), one kind. Finder A cited the summary statement b03019 ('is parallel to the third side') and finder B the heading EMA66 for it, but the reconciler's merged evidence for this objective is exercises only (its note says it left out 'the cited intro, heading and Ex7-8:22a evidence' and is silent on the summary quote; it did carry b03019 for lo-1 and lo-4), so the independent evidence check never examined them for this objective. G1 can add no evidence (it can approve, edit the wording, drop, or place items), and re-running the evidence check is a model call outside this task. Rule 1 needs two different kinds, so the objective is dropped and each of its 10 exercise items is re-homed to the objective of this lesson it practises (all to lo-1: the 'parallel to the third side' half of the theorem). Ids: the dropped objective is the second of four, so the run's fourth objective becomes lo:g10m7s4-1-2.

decisions.detail: 'Determine unknown angles, including angles in terms of a variable, in a triangle crossed by a line joining two mid-points, using the parallel lines the mid-point theorem gives.' Only exercise evidence (12 items); the other rule failure of this chapter (rule 1).
decisions.basis: ORCHESTRATOR (AI) RULING, not a human stamp and not in the auto-pass rule set: section 7.4 never teaches finding angles in a mid-point triangle. The method (mid-point theorem gives a parallel line, then corresponding angles, then the angle sum of a triangle) appears only inside the worked answers of exercises Ex7-7:5-6 and 15-16 and Ex7-8:21-22 and 27-28, which are exercise evidence; the corresponding-angle and angle-sum reasoning is taught in sections 7.1 and 7.2 (lessons g10m7s1-1 and g10m7s2-1), not here. The run's merged evidence for this objective is three exercises (Ex7-7:5a, 15a, 16a), one kind. Finder A cited the activity b02950 and finder B the summary statement b03019 ('is parallel to the third side') for it, but the reconciler's merged evidence for this objective is exercises only (its note says it left out the cited intro, heading and Ex7-8:22a evidence and is silent on the summary quote), so the independent evidence check never examined them for this objective; the theorem statement supports the parallel half only, not the angle work. G1 can add no evidence and re-running the check is a model call outside this task. Rule 1 needs two different kinds, so the objective is dropped and each of its 12 exercise items is re-homed to lo:g10m7s4-1-1, the objective whose theorem gives the parallel line every one of them starts from. Ids: the dropped objective is the third of four, so the run's fourth objective becomes lo:g10m7s4-1-2.
